Definition: , including the comparative τιμιώτερος, and the superlative τιμιώτατος from G5092; valuable, i.e. (objectively) costly, or (subjectively) honored, esteemed, or (figuratively) beloved:--dear, honourable, (more, most) precious, had in reputation.
BiblicalUsage: Precious is the word for what is costly and held dear. Paul pictures building on the foundation with gold, silver and precious stones, Peter speaks of the precious blood of Christ and the exceeding great and precious promises, and Luke notes that Gamaliel was had in reputation — held precious — among all the people.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word teaches me to weigh things rightly: what is precious is not what is common or loud, but what is costly, tested and kept. I hold that the blood and the promises Peter names are the measure by which everything else is priced.
